newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power flat to lower amid mild temps.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power flat to lower amid mild temps.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast finished Thursday flat to lower from Tuesday's levels amid outlook of mild temperatures in much of the region including Florida.
Wholesale power trading was light with many participants taking extended vacations for the Christmas holiday, market sources noted.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Friday were assessed in a $11.00-$13.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range, down sharply from Tuesday's $14.00-16.00 for Thursday.
Firm, off-peak electricity in northern TVA was notionally assessed near $9.00, compared with $8.00-9.00 Tuesday.
At the Georgia/Florida border, prices for firm, peak electricity in 16 hour blocks for Friday delivery held in a $17.00-18.00 range.
Firm, off-peak power for Thursday at the Ga./Fla. border was steady at $9.00.
In the Florida pennisula, 16-hour block power for firm delivery Friday was assessed in a $19.00-$21.00 range.
The mild weather outlook also pushed spot natural gas in south Texas lower. They slipped roughly 30 cents per million British thermal units from Tuesday to the $3.35-$3.45 area.
Friday temperatures in the Southeastern Electric Reliability Council (SERC) district, which excludes Florida, were expected to peak in 50-70 Fahrenheit degree range and bottom in the 30s-50s.
Friday temperatures in Florida were projected to peak in the 70s-80s and bottom in the 50s-60s.
